name: R01 evenBackslashesBefore: the walk capped at 1,048,576 characters
why: a run of 1,048,577 backslashes reads as even; the committed long-run rows stopped at 1,000,001 and the first tests let this through. Killed by the 1,048,575 to 1,048,577 rows

name: R02 atxClosingPandocStart: the hash walk capped at 262,144 characters
why: a run of a million `#` is cut short and answers the wrong index; no first-round row walked more than 200,000 `#` (the million-character near-miss rows end in `b`, so the walk is never entered). Killed by the 1,000,000-hash row

name: R03 atxClosingPandocStart: an odd-parity run of a million or more hashes refused
to: return end - start >= 2 && end - start < 1000000 ? start + 1 : -1;
why: `a \` and a million `#` answers -1 instead of 4. Killed by the same 1,000,000-hash row

name: R04 headingAttributeStart: the loop gives up after 150,000 failed braces
from: for (let open = text.indexOf("{", text.lastIndexOf("}", close - 1) + 1); open !== -1; open = text.indexOf("{", open + 1)) {
to: for (let open = text.indexOf("{", text.lastIndexOf("}", close - 1) + 1), tries = 0; open !== -1 && tries++ < 150000; open = text.indexOf("{", open + 1)) {
why: 250,000 escaped braces and then the real one answers -1; the only first-round row that ran the loop long had the real brace LAST, after 100,000. Killed by the 250,000-and-0 row

name: R05 headingAttributeStart: after 1,000 failed braces the loop jumps to the last brace
from: for (let open = text.indexOf("{", text.lastIndexOf("}", close - 1) + 1); open !== -1; open = text.indexOf("{", open + 1)) {
to: for (let open = text.indexOf("{", text.lastIndexOf("}", close - 1) + 1), tries = 0; open !== -1; open = tries++ === 1000 ? text.lastIndexOf("{") : text.indexOf("{", open + 1)) {
why: right only when the real brace is the last one; 1,500 escaped braces, the real one, then 1,500 more answers a different index. Killed by the 1,500-and-1,500 row

name: R06 headingAttributeStart: the trailing blanks trimmed again for every brace
why: every answer is the same; 50,000 failing braces and 100,000 trailing blanks cost 5e9 steps (23 s here at a load of 10; 82 s in the review at a load of 100 to 130). No first-round row held both a long run of failing braces and a long run of trailing blanks (each held one or the other). Killed by the clock row on the pair

name: R07 headingAttributeStart: the previous closing brace searched for within 300,000 characters only
why: a block with a body of 1,000,000 characters answers -1 instead of 2: the search for the `{` starts too late. Killed by the million-character block row

name: R08 buildHeading: the closing run located in the text with every Unicode space trimmed
why: `trimEnd()` also removes a no-break space, a form feed and a byte-order mark, which `[ \t]*$` does not call blank: `# C#` and a no-break space loses its `#`. The enumerations call the functions directly and the first wiring rows held no trailing Unicode space. Killed by the five no-break-space wiring rows

name: R09 headingAttributeStart: an escaped brace past index 3,000,000 accepted
why: SURVIVES ON PURPOSE: a cap family has no closable end. Every row stops at some largest size (here a million characters of block or of backslashes, and 250,000 escaped braces), so a cap set one size above it is never seen; R01 to R07 are the caps that sat just above the first round's sizes and the new rows close them
